prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best candidate (c013) clamps the per-net weight cap at 8.0; c015 already tested relaxing it to 11.2, so instead I make the conservative opposite refinement — tighten the cap modestly (x0.7 → 5.6) to further spread weight across many moderately-critical nets, which is the mechanism that drove c013's TNS-heavy gains (60% of the score).
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.412 robust(mean-std)=+0.105 min_case=+0.108 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.122 dWNS=+9.6% dTNS=+14.0% overflow~134
  bp-ng45: score=+0.108 dWNS=+3.9% dTNS=+15.3% overflow~108
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.182 dWNS=+18.9% dTNS=+17.5% overflow~128
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis held: tightening the cap to 5.6 improved all three cases, with robust mean +0.105 and all valid. Gains are TNS-heavy (bp-ng45 +15.3%, bp_fe +17.5%) plus strong WNS on bp_fe (+18.9%), consistent with spreading weight across many moderately-critical nets. ariane133 shows the smallest WNS gain (+9.6%) but solid TNS (+14.0%). Next step: sweep the cap between 5.6 and 8.0 (e.g., 6.4, 7.2) to locate the optimum, since c015's relaxation to 11.2 and this tightening both helped—suggesting the current 8.0 is not near the true optimum.
